subject: Peregrine Health — Post-call: SLOs, topology choices & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya R. <maya.r@peregrinehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Peregrine Health — Post-call: SLOs, topology choices & next steps

Hi Maya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the technical items we agreed to validate in the POC. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level goals (your priority order)
- Real-time triage in clinician UI (sub-200ms perceived latency for short prompts)
- Nightly batch scoring for record enrichment (throughput-oriented, cost sensitivity)
- Data residency in us-east VPC + KMS-managed keys

Pain points you shared
- Current in-house model has unpredictable p99 latency spikes under burst traffic.
- On-prem infra teams don't have an inference stack tuned for KV caching / long-contexts.
- Procurement needs a clear capacity & pricing estimate for a pilot.

Key SLOs we discussed (POC targets)
- Interactive endpoint (chat/completion): p50 ~40ms, p95 <120ms, p99 <220ms for 32-token responses; tail is main concern.
- Sustained throughput goal for POC: ~250 concurrent users (95th percentile concurrency) => ~1800 RPS of short prompts (~avg 16 tokens generation).
- Batch scoring: target 200k documents overnight; throughput-first with >=80% utilization on dedicated capacity.

Model & topology notes
- Recommended model baseline: open LLM 13B quantized (q4_0/q8_0) for interactive; fallback to a 7B variant when we need lower-cost routing.
- Topology sketch (attached): Dedicated cluster in us-east with autoscale buffer + hosted fallback in another region for burst spikes. KV cache pinned to dedicated pool to reduce warm-token latency.
- Kernel/infra optimizations: narrow attention kernels, dynamic batching window 8-12ms, per-route prefix caching for templated prompts.

POC asks we agreed to validate
1) Provide a representative prompt set + 1 week of traffic trace (anonymized) — you
2) Confirm dataset residency & KMS/GovCloud constraints — procurement
3) POC start target: week of 2027-02-14; duration: 3 weeks
4) Redwood to deliver: SLO Matrix (attached), topology sketch (attached), capacity cost estimate for pilot and steady-state.

Attachments: peregrine_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO targets + measurement plan), topology_sketch_v2.pdf (deployment sketch and failover paths).

Next steps (short):
- Maya: share anonymized traffic and any compliance checklist items by 2027-02-03.
- Alex/Jordan/Soojin: produce capacity estimate + POC runbook by 2027-02-07.

Thanks — will follow up with a 1-page mutual action plan tomorrow.

—
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Peregrine Health — Post-call: SLOs, topology choices & next steps

Thanks Alex — that looks right. Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) On the interactive SLOs, the p99 number seems aggressive but acceptable for the pilot if you can demonstrate a stable tail with KV caching. Our current spikes hit ~600–800ms p99 during business hours.
2) For model choice, we absolutely need a deterministic fallback path. If the 13B is unavailable, route to 7B with a short-form instruction template — acceptable tradeoff.
3) Procurement asked if the pilot estimate can include a 30% buffer for burst days.

We'll extract a 72-hour trace with sample prompts and share by EOD 2027-02-02. Also attaching the internal compliance note re: KMS (we will share the full doc on Friday).

Maya

Subject: Re: Fwd: Peregrine Health — Post-call: SLOs, topology choices & next steps

Ack — I'll start the topology draft today. Preliminary calls/assumptions I'll encode:

- Baseline infra: 4 x A100-equivalent nodes in dedicated pool for interactive traffic (shard across 2 availability zones).
- KV cache: 256GB shared cache with warmup pinning for top-100 templates; aim to reduce p99 by ~40–60ms in initial runs.
- Autoscale policy: scale at sustained CPU/GPU utilization >70% for 30s; add burst pool that can spin up hosted fallback instances in ~45s.
- Quantization plan: start with q8_0 for balanced perf/cost; include q4_0 option if memory permits and tail still problematic.

I'll attach a first-pass diagram and a short risk register. Jordan — ping me if you want any perf data points for cost calc.

-Soojin
